notes: Built 2026-09-25 from Wikipedia 'Results by constituency' tables on the 2026 TN/KL/PY Legislative Assembly election articles (parsed via bs4, handling rowspan District cells), cross-checked against the Kerala Legislative Assembly page's 'Current seats by alliance' table, the Puducherry Legislative Assembly page's dated (as on 25 September 2026) member table, and the '16th Puducherry Assembly' page. TN (234 seats, all filled at the 4 May 2026 count) now has 7 vacancies: 6 AIADMK MLAs (Madurantakam, Dharapuram, Perundurai, Karur, Viralimalai, Ambasamudram) resigned May-June 2026 after defecting to TVK, and CM C. Joseph Vijay (TVK) vacated Tiruchirappalli East (won both it and Perambur, retained Perambur). By-elections for Madurantakam and Dharapuram are scheduled 6 October 2026 (counting 9 October); the other 5 TN seats' by-election was TBD/under a Madras High Court stay as of 2026-09-25 (final hearing 28 Sept 2026) -- source: '2026-2031 Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly By-Polls' Wikipedia page plus Google News RSS (The New Indian Express, ETV Bharat, Times of India, 7-8 Sept 2026). KL (140 seats) had no vacancies found as of 2026-09-25 (confirmed via Google News search that the 6 October by-poll round covers only TN, Puducherry and West Bengal seats, not Kerala); one winner (Mani C. Kappan, Pala) had his party corrected from IND to Kerala Democratic Party (KDP) per the assembly's own current-composition table, since the 2026 election-results table listed him as Independent. PY (33 seats = 30 elected + 3 centrally-nominated) has 1 elected vacancy (Thattanchavady, CM N. Rangaswamy retained his other seat Mangalam instead) with the same 6 October by-election round, plus all 3 nominated MLA seats are recorded here as vacant/unconfirmed: neither the Puducherry Legislative Assembly page, the 16th Puducherry Assembly page, nor a Google News RSS search turned up named appointees for the 16th Assembly (the last confirmed nominations -- 3 BJP members re-notified July 2025 -- were for the outgoing 15th Assembly and resigned/lapsed around the 2026 dissolution); the assembly's own 'Party position' table does provisionally count 'Nominated: 3' within the NDA total of 21, so treat this as an open gap, not a confirmed vacancy -- flagged confidence:low per instructions rather than inventing names. Party abbreviation ADMK normalized to AIADMK per the requested standard list; all other party abbreviations (TVK, AINRC, LJK, NMK, KEC, KEC(J), RMPI, CMP, RSP, RJD, IUML, VCK, PMK, DMDK, AMMK, IND) are used as given by Wikipedia/the assembly's own tables since they are not in the standard list but are the correct, real abbreviations for these parties. Neither TN, KL nor PY currently has a Legislative Council.
